children.text: Mount Hibok-Hibok is an active volcano rising 1,332m in the middle of Camiguin Island. Starting at Ardent Hot Spring, the trail crosses jungle and a volcanic-rock ridge to the crater and summit, making it one of the best-known treks in the central and southern Philippines. A DENR permit and a local guide are required.
Mount Hibok-Hibok is the highest volcano on Camiguin, the island floating in the sea north of Mindanao. It is a stratovolcano standing
above sea level, with a base roughly
10km

across. Camiguin's best-known sights, including Katibawasan Falls, Ardent Hot Spring and White Island, all sit on terrain and heat created by this volcano, so anyone touring the island ends up looking up at its summit at least once.

The mountain is protected as part of the Timpoong-Hibok-Hibok Natural Monument. According to recent articles it was designated an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2015 and covers more than 2,200 hectares, including rainforest, a crater lake, waterfalls and hot springs. For that reason you cannot simply climb it on your own: a DENR (Department of Environment and Natural Resources) permit and a local guide are basic requirements. The rules reduce the chance of visitors getting lost or wandering into dangerous areas, and the guide fees also bring income to local residents.

Knowing the history changes how the mountain looks. Between 1871 and 1875, lava flowed from a fissure near Catarman and destroyed the town, and the 1948–1951 eruptions caused heavy loss of life through landslides, poisonous gas and boiling lava. Estimates of the death toll differ widely, from several hundred to more than 3,000, but either way the event is still remembered by Camiguin's people. Today the Hibok-Hibok Volcano Observatory under PHIVOLCS (the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology) monitors the volcano with solar-powered automatic stations, and in April 2026 PHIVOLCS called rumors of an eruption fake news and stated the volcano is at Alert Level 0 (quiet).
The climb is demanding. The first
2 hours

or so is a steep ascent through jungle, followed by stretches of volcanic rock with almost no shade. Near the summit there are sharp rocks and pitcher plants (Nepenthes), and on clear days you can reportedly see White Island, Bohol, Surigao and Siquijor. Moderately experienced hikers can manage it with some fitness preparation, but the Philippine heat and humidity make it feel much harder than a mountain of the same height at home. For first-time visitors, we suggest staying at least 2 nights on Camiguin. On the first day, arrive, rest in Mambajao, check the DENR office and guide schedule, and take a light look at a waterfall or hot spring. Climb at dawn on the second day and relax in the hot spring in the afternoon. That way, if it rains or the permit is delayed, you still have a spare day. By contrast, arriving and climbing on the same day, rushed by ferry times, easily strains both your stamina and your safety. After the hike, combine the Sunken Cemetery and White Island to see the volcanic island from other angles, which makes the trip more meaningful.
Most day hikes start near Ardent Hot Spring in Mambajao, about
10 minutes
from town by motorcycle (habal-habal). Soaking in the hot spring after the hike is the classic way to finish the course. The entrance fee is reported to be around
, so confirm it locally.
For about the first
2 hours

after the start, steep steps and root-covered paths wind through dense forest. The shade keeps off the sun, but humidity is high and there may be leeches. Wear long sleeves and bring leech protection.

blocks.title: Volcanic-rock slopes and the crater rim

children.text: Where the forest ends, exposed volcanic-rock slopes appear and sulfur steam rises from the crater edge. Do not stay long near the crater, and go only as far as the point your guide sets.
On clear early mornings you can reportedly see White Island, Bohol, Surigao and Siquijor from the summit. Clouds often form in the afternoon, so the earlier you start, the better the view.

Some trip reports describe camping near the crater lake on a 2-day, 1-night trek, climbing to the summit before dawn for sunrise and then coming back down. However, the campsite near the lake has flooded in heavy rain, so check the weather carefully.
Near the summit you can see highland plants such as pitcher plants (Nepenthes alata). It is a protected area, so do not dig up or pick plants, and carry all your trash back down.

Strong hikers do a traverse that starts in the village of Yumbing, passes the DENR outpost, the crater and the summit, and comes down toward Ardent. Because it is a one-way route, arrange transport and a guide in advance.

A guide does more than show the way: they watch PHIVOLCS updates and the weather to decide whether to go up. If clouds hang low or the crater steam is stronger than usual, they may shorten the route or turn back, so respect that judgment. Many guides speak English, and it is best to settle the exact fee and schedule clearly before you set out.

items.title: Day hike
items.subtitle: Round trip from Ardent Hot Spring

children.text: Get your permit at the DENR office in Mambajao and meet your guide. Permit hours differ by office, so it is safest to visit the day before and check.
Ride a motorcycle to Ardent Hot Spring. The ride takes about
10 minutes
Start the jungle ascent. Walk slowly at a steady pace.
Pass the volcanic-rock section and arrive at the crater rim. Rest with snacks and water.
Reach the summit. Enjoy the view and take photos before the clouds roll in.
Begin the descent. Take care of your knees and ankles on the way down.
Return to Ardent Hot Spring, loosen your muscles in the hot spring, and head back to town.
Sources differ widely on timing, from 3–5 hours to the summit and 6–10 hours round trip. It varies with fitness and weather, so decide with your guide.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night camping course
items.subtitle: A night at the crater lake

children.text: Get your permit, set out, and keep climbing toward the crater lake.
Arrive near the crater lake and pitch your tents.
Eat dinner and sleep early. There may be rats and leeches, so seal your food.
Wake before dawn and start the summit push. The last section has ropes and rocks.
Watch the sunrise and the view from the summit.
Break camp and descend.
Camping must follow your guide and DENR rules, and the rules may change often, so check the latest notices.
Flying from Manila to Cagayan de Oro (Laguindingan Airport, CGY) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
From the airport, take a bus or van to Balingoan Port, then board the ferry to Benoni Port on Camiguin. The ferry takes about
1 to 1.5 hours
and the fare is reported as about
in 2026 (terminal fee may or may not be included, depending on the operator); fares shift with fuel and season, so confirm locally.
Direct flights from Manila or Cebu to Camiguin Airport (CGM) are sometimes available, but schedules change often, so check the airline's announcements.
Allow a full day for the land trip from Cagayan de Oro to Balingoan plus the ferry; that is the safe plan.
From Benoni Port to Mambajao, take a van or tricycle.
From central Mambajao to the Ardent Hot Spring trailhead it is about
10 minutes
by motorcycle (habal-habal), and the fare, usually between
, is negotiated.
You can tour the island's ring road by motorcycle or rental car.
The best time to hike is the dry season, from December to May. The trail is relatively dry and the summit views are often clear.
In the rainy season the trail is slippery, clouds easily cover the summit, and the campsite can flood. In any season, the rule is to start early in the morning.

rows: Best hiking period, but permits and rooms get crowded over the year-end holidays

The night before the hike, staying in central Mambajao or near Ardent Hot Spring makes the early start easier. The town has guesthouses and budget-friendly hotels, and there are many resorts along the coast. Guides are usually arranged a day ahead through your lodging or the town tourist office.

Buy packed meals and water at shops in town beforehand. Camiguin is famous for the sweet fruit lanzones, so if it is in season, enjoy some as a snack after the hike. You can also ask your guide to arrange meals.

After the hike, you can have a hearty meal at restaurants in central Mambajao with local seafood, grilled chicken and rice dishes. Prices are generally not high, and since Camiguin is a quiet island, many places close early at night, so eat dinner early.
A permit and guide are required, so check and book in advance the day before at the DENR office or tourist office in Mambajao.
Plan to set out at 5–6 AM so you reach the summit before the clouds form.
Bring at least 2 liters of water per person, plus plenty of snacks and trail food.
Prepare hiking shoes (or shoes with good grip), long sleeves, a hat, sunscreen and a rain jacket.
There may be leeches and rats, so bring repellent and containers to seal your food.
Loosening your muscles in the Ardent hot spring after the descent reduces pain the next day.
Carry all trash back down, and do not collect plants.
Fees for permits and guides vary by report, so confirm the official rates when you arrive.
If your knees or ankles are weak, trekking poles are a big help on the descent.
Carry plenty of cash. Cards are often not accepted at the trail entrance and the hot spring.
Hibok-Hibok is an active volcano. Check PHIVOLCS announcements before you go; if the alert level is raised, the hike may be suspended.
At present (PHIVOLCS statement of April 2026) it is at Alert Level 0, but conditions can change, so check the latest notice before departure.
Sulfur steam and toxic gas can come from near the crater, so do not linger.
The section just before the summit has rocks and ropes and is slippery, and dangerous in rain.
If heavy rain is expected, avoid camping at the crater lake.
Do not hike alone; stay with your guide.
The waterfalls, hot springs and beaches across the island are worth more than a day. See the Camiguin entry for details.
A white sand island about
20–30 minutes
from Mambajao by boat. In good weather the ridge of Hibok-Hibok appears as the backdrop.

blocks.title: Sunken Cemetery and Guiob Church Ruins

children.text: The cemetery and church site that sank in the 1871 eruption remain, which helps you understand the volcano's history.
The gateway city to Camiguin; from here you travel overland to Balingoan Port.
